claim: Loop length for the 30 m design span is 60.4 m
law: Two legs plus half a wrap of the rope centre line (56 mm radius) round each sheave

claim: Peak hand pull to haul a 30 m gillnet with 10 kg of catch is about 200 N
law: Coulomb friction (0.6) and lift of catch, weed and a fifth of the wet net up a 27 degree bank edge, plus half the water drag; still water. Sensitivity: 241 N in a 0.3 m/s current, 243 N at friction 0.9

claim: Pull to set the net (loop and net paying out at 0.5 m/s) is about 43 N
law: Rope friction on the ground, lead line friction on the bed and drag, through two blocks at 0.95 each

claim: A person can make a 200 N peak hand-over-hand pull on a rope, briefly, twice a day
law: Manual pulling forces of the working population (ISO 11228-2 method, to assess for the users); the peak lasts the few seconds the catch crosses the bank edge
check: No population data for the partner fishers; the R3 trial measures the pull with a spring scale

claim: The weak link never breaks in normal use: its lowest release is at least twice the largest normal load
law: Lowest release 510 N over the largest load in normal use (setting, 62 N); hauling is by the net's near end by hand, so the far link only drags the loop (18 N) and no haul load passes a link

claim: A braided cord loop can be chosen to release between 500 and 700 N (600 N plus or minus 15 %)
law: Breaking strength scatter of one batch of braided polyester cord; calibrated by pulling three samples (BKH-BLD-001 3.7)
check: Batch scatter to measure at TRL 4 on CalRig

claim: A seized net cannot load the far end beyond 1.5 kN (both legs at the link's highest release)
law: Statics of the far block: two legs at 690 N

claim: A set gillnet in a 0.3 m/s current stays below the weak link's lowest release
law: Drag 0.5 rho v^2 Cd A on the twine (solidity about 0.0125 for 0.25 mm twine at 40 mm bar) and on the head and foot ropes, Cd 1.2; a clean net reaches the link's release at 0.76 m/s, so the station is for still to slow water

claim: The 10 mm polyester stays carry the 3 kN bank load with a factor of 5 or more on breaking strength
law: Stay tension from statics of two splayed stays (2.08 kN); 10 mm three-strand polyester 1,590 kg (15.6 kN) minimum break load (Marlow), 85 % at the eye splice

claim: The post does not buckle under the stays' downward pull
law: Euler buckling, 48.3 x 3.2 tube 1.0 m, pinned both ends, against 2.6 kN

claim: The 350 mm foot plate bears on soft wet soil (10 kPa) with a factor of 2
law: Undrained bearing capacity Nc su with Nc 5.14 (Terzaghi, strip; conservative for a square plate)

claim: Each 250 mm screw anchor holds its stay with a factor of 2 in soft soil of 10 kPa
law: Helical anchor breakout Q = Fc su A, Fc 9 at H/D at the critical ratio 0.107 su + 2.5 (Das, Earth Anchors), loaded along its axis; at the creep threshold, so the TRL 4 pull test settles it; factor 1.07 if the bank were 5 kPa

claim: The pad eye, stay lugs and collar lug meet the pin-plate geometry rules
law: EN 1993-1-8 Table 3.9 type A: a >= F gM0 / (2 t fy) + 2 d0 / 3, c >= F gM0 / (2 t fy) + d0 / 3, S235, 1.5 x working load; least ratio of the three plates

claim: The near block's working load limit covers both legs at 1.5 kN
law: Catalogue working load limit 500 kg (4.9 kN) against 3.0 kN

claim: The far stake, driven 3.5 m, holds 1.5 kN with a factor of 2 in soft and very soft mud
law: Broms lateral capacity in clay, the lesser of the short pile (soil fails) and the long pile (stake yields at its S355 plastic moment); very soft mud at 1.0 m of water governs; at the top pin hole (1.2 m of water) 2.51 in soft mud and 1.91 in very soft mud, so the top hole is not used in very soft beds (D-S7)

claim: The stake stays elastic at the R5 load
law: Bending at the largest moment, M = H (e + 1.5 d + 0.5 f), elastic modulus of the 76.1 x 3.6 tube, water 1.2 m deep at the top hole; limit 355 / 1.5 MPa; no corrosion allowance (S23)

claim: A 76.1 mm stake can be driven 3.5 m into a soft bed from a boat with a post driver or sledge
law: Driving resistance of soft clay is low; the cap disc and driving cap spread the blows (BKH-BLD-001 step 6)
check: Driving effort and verticality to confirm at the trial site; a firm layer would stop it short of 3.5 m (to confirm by probing)

claim: The loop rope keeps a factor of 5 on its working tension at the end of a season
law: 20 kN taken for 12 mm three-strand polysteel (12-strand polysteel is 2,740 kg, Marlow), 85 % at the splices with both ends of each half spliced (D-S6; a hitch at about 60 % gave 4.0), half lost to sun: factor 5.67
check: Rests on the UV loss of S19 and the bought rope's breaking strength; both to confirm

claim: UV-stabilised polysteel rope loses no more than half its strength in one tropical season
law: Photo-oxidation of polypropylene and polyethylene in sunlight; the stabiliser and the season's dose set the loss. The factor stays above 2 unless 80 % is lost
check: Loss rate for the rope bought to measure in the season pilot (R7)

claim: The polysteel loop floats in fresh and brackish water
law: Density of the polypropylene and polyethylene blend about 0.93 g/cm3 (rope maker's data) against water at 1.00 to 1.01

claim: The 100 mm sheave suits 12 mm fibre rope at this load
law: Sheave to rope diameter ratio 8.33 on the tread, at the commonly quoted minimum of about 8 for fibre rope (source to confirm with the rope maker); working tension under 8 % of breaking strength
check: Ratio on the margin of the guidance; bending wear observed in the season pilot

claim: Bushed nylon sheaves last a season in silty water
law: Abrasive wear of a plain bush by silt; 720 passes a season at low load
check: Bush wear to record in the season pilot (R7)

claim: The painted steel post and stake, galvanised rigging and stainless stop pin last several seasons in fresh or brackish water
law: Corrosion of carbon steel at a waterline and in mud; the small stainless bolt is the cathode against a large painted steel area, the favourable galvanic ratio
check: Corrosion rate in the trial water to confirm; inspect the stake at the waterline each season (BKH-RSK-001)

claim: Working 5 m or more back from the water's edge meets published crocodile-safety advice for fishing
law: Northern Territory Government, Be Crocwise: "Stand at least five meters back from the water's edge while fishing" (checked 2026-10-25)
check: The layout gives 5.0 m (R11); the local wildlife authority's advice for the site may ask for more

claim: Setting and hauling from the bank removes most of the fishers' exposure
law: At Kariba 58 % of 60 sampled attacks happened while fishing (Matanzima et al., Oryx); exposure while wading and setting is removed, exposure at the bank is not
check: The share of fishing attacks that happen while wading, rather than from canoes or the bank, is not known for the trial site

claim: Nets set and hauled on the loop catch about as many fish as nets set by wading
law: Gillnet catch depends on where and how long the net is set; the loop sets the net along one line from the bank
check: Catch per set to compare in field trials with partner fishers (TRL 5)

claim: A full haul and reset takes about 6 minutes without clearing fish
law: Rope speed and the fixed handling steps

claim: Each screw anchor holds about 4.4 kN
law: Q = Fc su A in N with su in Pa and A in m2

claim: Every part of the design fits its neighbours: the D3 model has no interference, and the stay chain closes within the turnbuckle's take-up
law: cad_check interference (no overlap over 5 mm3) and the stay chain: 1440 mm lug to anchor eye less 329 mm of shackles and turnbuckle leaves 1111 mm between thimbles (the stay was drawn 1,440 mm); check: difference from the 1,110 mm made, against the 75 mm half take-up

claim: Two people can lift the heaviest part (the far stake, 33.2 kg) upright in a boat
law: ISO 11228-1 reference mass 25 kg per person in ideal conditions; a team lift counts for less than the sum, and a 5 m tube in a boat is awkward
check: 16.6 kg each; lowered on a rope through the top cross hole from the boat side, decided by Amish 2026-10-25 (BKH-DEC-001 O-7); PR-014 met on paper, to confirm in the TRL 4 drill

claim: Option B: the 8 mm wire track cable carries a seized net at mid-span with a factor of 5
law: Cable tension T = F L / (4 s) + w L^2 / (8 s), the 690 N link release taken as a downward pull at mid-span of 30 m with 1.0 m sag: 5.5 kN; 8 mm galvanised wire rope about 40 kN minimum breaking force (catalogue order, to confirm), 80 % at grip terminations

claim: Option B: the far mast's guy anchor holds the cable's pull in a soft bed
law: Guy tension 10.2 kN at about 58 degrees; one 250 mm helix holds 4.4 kN at 10 kPa and 2.2 kN at 5 kPa (S12 method), so the guy needs about 4.6 to 9.3 times one anchor for a factor of 2; four anchors on a spreader give 1.7 at 10 kPa, a 2.5 m sag (4 m masts) 1.07 on one anchor. Fix sized on paper: a buried timber deadman of about 20 kN or a site with a firm bed; not modelled because option B is not carried forward
check: Fails; the tensioned span multiplies the net-end pull about eight times into the guy

claim: Option B: the carriage wheels run on the 8 mm wire without wearing it out in a season
law: Wheel groove 9 mm wide for an 8 mm wire; wheel to wire ratio 60 / 8 = 7.5, far below the ratios wire rope makers ask for sheaves the wire bends round, but the carriage rolls along the wire rather than bending it
check: Wire and wheel wear to assess if option B is carried forward

claim: Option B: masts 2.6 m and 3.0 m high keep the cable and carriage clear of the water
law: Sag of 1.0 m at 30 m with the carriage at mid-span leaves about 1.0 m over the water
check: To confirm with the site's flood level

claim: Option C: the hand line raises a wet 3 m net with 10 kg of catch at no more than 250 N
law: Moments about the pivot: boom 9.6 kg/m over 8 m and 3 m arms, 25 kg of net, spreaders and catch at the tip, six 19 kg blocks and a 20 kg basket at 2.55 m; pull at 3 m. Fix sized on paper: two more blocks and a second line to lower the empty net; not modelled because option C is not carried forward

claim: Option C: the 40 mm pivot pin carries the boom, counterweight and net
law: Simply supported over the 710 mm between head plates, 2.7 kN at mid-span; S235, limit 235 / 1.5 MPa

claim: Option C: a 3 m lift net 5 m out catches enough fish for a household
law: Shore lift nets work where fish come close inshore, often to a light at night; reach 5 m beyond the edge
check: Catch to assess with partner fishers; changes the fishing method

claim: Option C: the stayed 8 m boom is stiff enough to hold the net level over the water
law: Unstayed, the root moment is about 5.0 kN m against an elastic moment of 11.5 kN m (S355), so strength holds, but the tip sags about 264 mm; the king post stays stiffen it
check: Stay loads and tip sag with the stays to calculate if option C is carried forward
